newsitem.title: USA: Iowa governor set to sign tax-related bills.
newsitem.headline: Iowa governor set to sign tax-related bills.

text.p: Iowa Gov. Terry Branstad is scheduled to sign into law Thursday a bill calling for a 10 percent cut in the state's income tax rate and another measure that would allow local governments to collect property taxes from publicly-owned race tracks, the governor's spokesman said Wednesday.
Eric Woolson said the bill signing is scheduled for Thursday afternoon.
The legislature gave final approval to the across-the-board income tax cut Monday night, Woolson said, adding that the $200 million annual cost of the cut would be funded with state surplus funds.

Branstad will also sign a bill allowing property taxes to be collected from the Polk County-owned Prairie Meadows Race Track and Casino in Altoona and from the Dubuque Greyhound Park and Casino, Woolson said.

Both tracks were financed with bonds, although Dubuque paid off its bonds in 1992 and Polk County expects to have enough money set aside by the end of the month to defease bonds it issued when they mature or become callable.
The measure is expected to cost the Prairie Meadows track $1.5 million a year and the Dubuque track $200,000 annually, according to officials.
